## Google Ads or SEO?
https://minarankstudio.com/blog/google-ads-or-seo/

One buys you today. The other buys you next year.
The comparison every owner runs before spending, usually with somebody selling one of the two answering it.
By Henri Sila · 22 August 2026
The difference in one line
Ads put you at the top of a page you have not earned, for as long as you keep paying. Search earns the position and keeps it after the spending stops.
Everything else is detail, and most arguments about the two are really arguments about which of those two problems you have this quarter.
When paying is clearly right
When you need customers before search could possibly deliver them. A new business, a seasonal window, a location opening next month.
Also when what you sell is urgent. Somebody with a burst pipe is not comparing five results, and being first for that minute is worth more than being respected for a year.
When it is clearly wrong
When the page they land on cannot convert them. Paying to send strangers to a site with no prices, no address and a form nobody has tested is buying traffic to prove a point.
Also when the budget is small enough that the money disappears before anybody learns anything from it. A budget that cannot survive a fortnight of testing teaches you nothing.
The part nobody mentions
They are not really alternatives. Ads reveal, in weeks, which words actually bring people who buy, and that is the most expensive thing to learn any other way.
Run for a month, read honestly, they tell you what the slower work should aim at. That is worth the money even if you never advertise again.
What we would do with a small budget
Fix the page first, because both routes end there. Then advertise narrowly, on the few words closest to a purchase, and read what comes back.
Then spend the slow work on whatever the ads proved people want. The order matters more than the split.
Questions worth asking
Can we do both at once?
Yes, and it is often the right answer, but only after the page they arrive on is worth arriving at. Doing both badly costs twice and teaches you half as much.
Do ads help our normal rankings?
No. Paying does not move the unpaid results, and Google has said so repeatedly. What ads do is tell you which words are worth the slower effort, which is a different kind of help and a real one.
What about Meta ads instead?
Different job. Search catches somebody already looking for you. Meta puts you in front of somebody who was not looking, which suits things people buy on sight and suits emergency plumbing very badly.
How small is too small a budget?
When a single click costs a noticeable share of the daily spend, you are not running a campaign, you are buying a few visitors. At that point the money does more on the site itself.
If we stop advertising, do we lose everything?
You lose the traffic immediately, which is the honest cost of renting the position. What you keep is what you learned and whatever the slower work built in the meantime, which is the argument for doing both.
Tell us what you sell and where, and we will say which of the two we would start with and why.
Get a free audit.

## Why the fastest reply wins the job
https://minarankstudio.com/blog/whoever-answers-first/

The job goes to whoever answers first.
A homeowner with no heating calls 3 numbers and books the one that picks up. The ad is the smaller half.
By Henri Sila · 14 August 2026
The short answer
In the trades, the ad does not win the job. A homeowner with no heating calls 3 numbers and books the one that picks up. Everything you spend on being found is decided in the minutes after somebody finds you.
The shape of an emergency customer
Somebody whose boiler died is not researching. They are ringing down a list, and the list is short. Being on it is what the ads buy. Staying on it for longer than one unanswered call is up to you.
This is why 2 firms can run the same ad, pay the same money, and get completely different months. The difference was never the ad.
What we built for a heating business
ProAffy generates enquiries for heating and cooling firms, so this problem is their whole business. The site we built for them is shaped around speed of response rather than looks: the page's one job is to start the conversation now.
The guarantee sits plainly on the page instead of buried in terms, because a customer in a hurry does not read terms, and trust has about a sentence to happen in.
The 90 seconds that decide it
Most of the result is decided in the 90 seconds after somebody taps. Does the page load, does it say the thing they need, is there one obvious way to reach you, and does that way actually get answered.
Every step is fixable, and none of them is more ad spend. Which is why we will tell you when the honest fix is your reply time, not your budget.
Ask us how fast your last enquiry got an answer. If you do not know, that is the answer.

## Facebook ads for estate agents
https://minarankstudio.com/blog/estate-agents/

The portal already has the buyers. You are competing for the seller.
Every agent in town advertises the same flats to the same buyers on the same site. None of that decides who gets the next instruction.
By Henri Sila · 14 August 2026
The short answer
Buyers go to the portal, because that is where every property is. Your listing competes there on price and photographs and very little else.
The seller is the scarce thing. Winning that is a different job and almost nobody spends money on it.
Why the portal is not your marketing
Paying to list on a portal puts you in a row with every rival, on a page the portal owns, in front of a buyer who will never learn your name. It is distribution and it is necessary.
It is not a reason anybody would choose you to sell their flat, which is the only decision that grows an agency.
What a seller is actually deciding
Somebody thinking of selling wants to know what their place is worth, how long it will take, and whether you have sold anything like it nearby.
They usually think about it for months before ringing anybody. That long quiet period is the whole opportunity, and it is not on the portal.
Where the money should go instead
Pages about the streets you actually sell in, what went recently and roughly for what. Ads aimed at the people who own in those streets rather than at everyone looking to buy.
That is a smaller audience and a much shorter distance to an instruction.
The photographs are the product
A seller judges you by the last listing you published, because it is the only evidence of how theirs will look. Bad photographs do not just cost you that sale. They cost you the next instruction, from somebody who saw them and quietly decided.
Questions worth asking
My listings are on the portals. Why my own site?
The portals sell you to buyers. Your site sells you to sellers, and sellers are where the money is. That is a different page making a different argument.
Should I advertise properties or myself?
Properties get the clicks. Advertising yourself gets the instructions. Run the property ads if you want the traffic, but the campaign that pays is the one aimed at somebody deciding who to list with.
What happens to a listing after it sells?
Keep it, marked as sold. A page of what you sold is the argument for instructing you, and deleting it throws away the only proof you have.
How fast do I have to reply?
Faster than you think. Enquiries go to whoever answers first far more often than to whoever is best, and most of them arrive outside office hours.
What decides the price?
Whether you want the site, the ads or both, how many languages, and whether the listings come out of a system you already use. Ads on their own are a small setup.
Tell us where your last 3 instructions came from, and we will tell you whether the portal had anything to do with it.

## The money numbers a small shop should track
https://minarankstudio.com/blog/four-lines-that-were-five/

The 4 money lines that were really 5.
A stacked chart has no total of its own to disagree with, so it lied quietly for weeks.
By Henri Sila · 14 August 2026
The short answer
Software a business runs on does not usually fail loudly. It fails by quietly leaving something out, and the business believes the number because it came off a screen.
Here is one we found in our own build, what it cost, and why we now check for it differently.
A chart that could not be wrong, and was
The system tracks money in separate lines so the owner can see which part of the business actually earns. A 5th line was added, and 5 charts carried on summing 4.
Nothing broke. Nothing looked odd. A stacked chart has no total of its own to disagree with, so the picture stayed plausible and the money quietly did not add up. It ran that way for a whole phase of work.
The guard that found it, and the one it could not
We wrote a check that searches the source for anywhere all 4 original lines are named together. It found the 5 charts immediately.
It could not find the 6th problem. One function named the 4 lines as an object spread over 4 lines of code, which looks nothing like a list to a text search.
The day a 5th line existed, that function threw and took the whole statistics panel down with it. A crawler that opens every screen and clicks everything found it in a minute. No amount of searching the text would have.
The replacement check asks the functions themselves whether every row carries every line. It catches the shape rather than the words.
Why this is the argument for custom software
The same shop had a second problem of the same family. Revenue and cash were the same number. They are not.
Money is earned when the watch goes back to the customer, and received when they actually pay. A month of big handovers and slow payers prints as a triumph while the till is empty.
A spreadsheet will never tell you that, because a spreadsheet has no opinion. It adds what you point it at.
A third: a watch sold whose price never synced counted as one watch and zero money. Unknown is not zero, so the count of items with no price now travels alongside the total and gets printed next to it.
What it does on an ordinary day
Stock, repair jobs, who owes what, and the month on one printable page. It works in a back room with thick walls and no signal, because the reference library is real pages rather than a call to a server. It costs nothing per month to run.
And it is wired to the shop's website: sell a watch over the counter and the site stops offering it about a minute later, without anybody touching a computer. That minute is not a figure of speech. It is a 60 second cache, and there is a test that fails if it drifts.
The whole build is on the Iglisi Watch page, and what we would build for a different trade is on the custom software page.
The part worth stealing
If a number on your screen has never disagreed with anything, it has never been checked. Find the place your system adds something up, and go and add it up by hand once. That is a free afternoon and it is how we found ours.
Tell us what you still count by hand every week. We will tell you whether it is worth building something, and we will say so when it is not.
Get a free audit.

## How we work

How we work, and what we will not do.
Everything here is written to be argued with. If you
disagree with any of it, we are probably not the right studio for you.
minarank studio works across search, AI search, websites, ads and
the software behind them, for small businesses in Albania, Italy and
anywhere else the work fits.
Evidence before opinion
Every job starts with the crawl, the code, the competitors and what people
are actually typing. Opinions are cheap and everyone in this industry has
several. We would rather show you the data that changed our mind.
One document, in plain language
What we would change, in what order, and why it matters. If it takes a
glossary to read, it is written badly. You should be able to hand it to
somebody who does not work in marketing and have them follow it.
We build it ourselves
Pages, schema, creative, software. Nothing gets handed to a third party
who loses 3 weeks and half the intent, and nothing gets handed to a junior
while you keep paying senior rates.
Numbers that are true
We report what moved and what did not. A month where nothing improved gets
reported as a month where nothing improved, with what we are changing
because of it.
What we will tell you for free
If your ad budget is too small to be worth managing, we will say so rather

answer is that you need a better offer rather than better marketing, that

English, Italian and Albanian. Work is delivered in the language your
customers are searching in, which for most of our clients is not English.
You do not have to take our word for any of this. minarank studio is listed
on TechBehemoths, which somebody else runs, and a profile we do not
control is worth more than a badge we drew ourselves.

Durres. Questions go to info@minarankstudio.com.

Is this one person or a team?
One person, and you always know which one. Henri Sila writes the

Do we need to be in Durres?
No. Most of this happens inside a browser and a document, and several
clients have never been in the same room as us. If you are near, we
come to you, because seeing the place usually changes the plan.
What if somebody already handles this for us?
Keep them, and take the audit as a second opinion. If what they are
doing is working, you get proof of it in writing. If it is not, you
get a list they can act on. Neither answer means hiring us.
What happens if we outgrow you?
It happens, and it is the good kind of problem. When a business
needs a team of specialists instead of one person, we say so rather
than stretch and hope. Handing over cleanly is part of the job.
Can we speak to somebody you have worked with?
Yes. Ask, and we introduce you to the client whose situation looks
most like yours. The work is public either way: each of them has a
page here saying what changed and what did not.

code. No account manager relaying it, and no junior practising on your site.
What does it cost?
Four things move it: how many pages, how many languages, whether the
site has to hold stock, bookings or payments, and whether the
photographs and text already exist. That is why the audit comes first
and costs nothing. You get the price with the plan, on one page, before
any work starts. Meta ads are a flat fee rather than a cut of what you
spend.

## What the words mean
https://minarankstudio.com/glossary/

What the words mean.
The jargon on this site, in plain language. If a word here is doing work you did not ask for, that is worth knowing before you pay anybody for it.
Every trade has words that keep outsiders out. Ours has more than most, and an agency that leaves them unexplained is not being technical, it is being hard to check.
These are the words we use on this site and what each one actually means. Nothing here is a promise about what any of them will do for you: that argument lives on the pages themselves.
SEO
Search engine optimisation: the work of making a site the thing Google shows when somebody searches for what you sell. It is not one job but several, and most of it is ordinary work done carefully.
GEO
Generative engine optimisation: the same idea aimed at ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity instead of a results page. It is young enough that anybody selling you certainty about it is selling you something.
AI search
Asking an assistant a question instead of typing keywords into Google. The answer names a few businesses and the person asking rarely checks further, which is why being one of them matters.
ranking
Where your page sits in a list of results. It moves by the day, differs by who is searching and from where, and a single number for it is always an average of many different answers.
map listing
The box with your shop, your hours and your reviews that appears above the ordinary results. For a business people walk into, it is usually seen more often than the website is.
Google Business Profile
The free account where you edit what the map listing says. The listing is what a customer sees; the profile is where you control it. Claiming it costs nothing and takes about twenty minutes.
times shown
How often your page appeared in front of somebody, whether or not they clicked. It measures reach and not interest, and rising numbers are the earliest sign anything is working.
clicks
How many people actually chose your result and arrived on your site. The only number on this list that corresponds to a real person deciding to visit you.
click rate
Clicks divided by times shown, as a percentage. It answers a narrower question than it looks: not whether people want what you sell, but whether your title and description earned the click.
audit
A read of a site against what search engines and readers need from it, written down. Ours names what is wrong, what it costs you and what we would do about it, in that order.
custom software
A tool built for one business instead of rented from a company that built it for everybody. Worth it when the way you work is the thing that makes you money, and not otherwise.
